gloss: inconvenient; not a good time; unfavorable

definitions.gloss: inconvenient; not a good time; to have a scheduling conflict
definitions.explanation: Used when a proposed time or arrangement does not work for someone due to their circumstances or schedule.
Used when a situation, fact, or outcome is unfavorable or embarrassing for someone, often something they would rather hide.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}い。
{都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}ければ、{別|べつ}の{日|ひ}にしましょう。
examples.english: If it's not convenient, let's pick another day.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}くなったので、{欠席|けっせき}させていただきます。
examples.english: Something has come up, so I'm afraid I won't be able to attend.

examples.japanese: {都合|つごう}の{悪|わる}い{事実|じじつ}は{隠|かく}す。
{自分|じぶん}に{都合|つごう}の{悪|わる}いことは{言|い}いたがらない。
examples.english: People don't like to talk about things that are unfavorable to them.

examples.japanese: その{情報|じょうほう}が{公|おおやけ}になると{都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}い{人|ひと}がいるらしい。
examples.english: Apparently there are people who would be in trouble if that information became public.

notes:
A very common expression used daily for declining invitations and describing scheduling conflicts. Also used to describe situations that are awkward or disadvantageous for someone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}い{日|ひ}: a day that doesn't work
- {都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}くなる: for something to come up (scheduling)
- {都合|つごう}の{悪|わる}い{話|はなし}: an inconvenient story; an awkward topic
- {自分|じぶん}に{都合|つごう}の{悪|わる}い: unfavorable to oneself

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不都合|ふつごう}な: inconvenient (adjective form) — more formal; often used in official or written contexts
- {都合|つごう}がつかない: cannot make time — specifically about scheduling; cannot arrange one's time
- {都合|つごう}がいい: convenient; a good time — the positive counterpart
